workflow.critical: NEVER fabricate test results — always run actual commands
Capture complete stdout and stderr output

step.action: Identify the correct test run command: - Jest: npx jest --verbose --coverage --json --outputFile=test-results.json - Vitest: npx vitest run --reporter=verbose --coverage - Pytest: python -m pytest -v --tb=long --cov --cov-report=json - Mocha: npx mocha --recursive --reporter spec - Go: go test -v -cover ./...

Check for: - Test configuration files (jest.config, vitest.config, pytest.ini) - Custom test scripts in package.json / Makefile - Required environment variables for testing - Test database setup requirements
Ensure test prerequisites: - Dependencies installed (npm install / pip install) - Test database available (if needed) - Environment variables set - Test fixtures/seed data loaded

check.action: Set up test database or use in-memory alternative

step.action: Run tests in order: 1. Unit tests first (fastest, most likely to pass) 2. Integration tests second 3. E2E tests last (slowest)
For each suite: - Execute the test command - Capture complete output (stdout + stderr) - Record execution time - Record pass/fail counts - Save raw output for analysis
If tests fail: - Do NOT stop — continue running remaining suites - Capture the full failure output including stack traces - Note which tests failed and which passed
Gather coverage reports: - Overall line coverage percentage - Per-file coverage breakdown - Uncovered lines and branches - Coverage comparison vs target from test strategy
Save previous results for regression comparison
